title: Pell Equations and Generalized Pell Orbits

items.title: Pell's equation
Generalized and negative Pell equations
The norm on the explicit order $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{D}]$
The Pell norm is multiplicative
items.strategy: Expand products in the explicit coordinate model $x + y\sqrt{D}$ and compare coefficients. The same expansion gives the star-product formula on coordinate pairs and proves norm multiplicativity without importing abstract field norm machinery.

items.title: Integral Pell solutions form an abelian group
items.strategy: Identify a solution of $x^2 - Dy^2 = 1$ with $x + y\sqrt{D}$. Closure and inverses come from the explicit multiplicative norm law, while commutativity is inherited from the coordinate multiplication formula in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{D}]$.

items.title: The complete quotients of $\sqrt{D}$ satisfy the $P_n,Q_n$ recurrence
items.strategy: Start from a normalized state $\alpha_n = (\sqrt{D} + P_n)/Q_n$ with $Q_n > 0$ and $Q_n \mid D - P_n^2$. Taking $a_n = \lfloor \alpha_n \rfloor$ and rationalizing $1/(\alpha_n-a_n)$ yields the next state $(P_{n+1}, Q_{n+1})$, while the positivity and divisibility conditions make the normalized state unique.

items.title: Convergents to $\sqrt{D}$ satisfy the norm identity
items.strategy: Insert the normalized next complete quotient into the continued-fraction tail formula for $\sqrt{D}$, clear denominators, and compare coefficients. The determinant identity for consecutive convergents then isolates $p_n^2 - Dq_n^2$ as $(-1)^{n+1}Q_{n+1}$.

items.title: The continued fraction of $\sqrt{D}$ has symmetric period ending in $2a_0$
items.strategy: Use the $P_n,Q_n$ recurrence to prove the bounds $0 < P_n < \sqrt{D}$ and $0 < Q_n < 2\sqrt{D}$ for $n \ge 1$, leaving only finitely many normalized states. Determinism forces a first repeated state, which must be $(a_0,1)$, and conjugating the backward recurrence reverses the intervening states and hence the digits.

items.title: Every Pell equation has a positive nontrivial integral solution
items.strategy: Apply the period-structure theorem and the convergent norm identity at the end of one full period. If the period length is even, the terminal convergent already has norm $1$; if it is odd, the terminal convergent has norm $-1$ and squaring it gives a norm-one solution.

items.title: Negative Pell is soluble exactly for odd period length
items.strategy: The symmetric period structure and the convergent norm identity show that an odd period yields a negative-Pell solution at the last convergent before the return state, and identify the least positive norm-one solution in each parity case. For the converse, apply NT-7's strict Legendre criterion to any positive solution of $x^2 - Dy^2 = -1$ so that it must appear among the convergents of $\sqrt{D}$.

items.title: The fundamental Pell solution
All positive Pell solutions are powers of the fundamental solution
items.strategy: Given a positive solution $\alpha$, choose the unique integer $k$ with $\varepsilon_D^k \le \alpha < \varepsilon_D^{k+1}$. The quotient $\alpha\varepsilon_D^{-k}$ is an integral norm-one element between $1$ and $\varepsilon_D$, so minimality of the fundamental solution forces it to equal $1$.

items.title: All integral Pell solutions are $\pm \varepsilon_D^k$
items.strategy: Among $\alpha$, $\alpha^{-1}$, $-\alpha$, and $-\alpha^{-1}$, exactly one lies in the positive cone. Apply the positive-solutions theorem there, then restore the sign and inverse data.

items.title: Pell-equivalence for generalized solutions
Generalized Pell solutions fall into finitely many Pell orbits
items.strategy: For a nonzero solution $\alpha$, choose the unique integer exponent that places the positive real embedding of $\alpha\varepsilon_D^{-k}$ in a fixed half-open logarithmic interval centered at $0$. The conjugate embedding is then $N/\alpha$, which gives explicit bounds on both coefficients and leaves only finitely many possible representatives.

items.title: Generalized Pell solubility is decidable by bounded search
items.strategy: Search the explicit rectangle from the orbit theorem and retain one representative from each orbit under multiplication by powers of $\varepsilon_D$. The search is finite and succeeds exactly when a solution exists.

items.title: One generalized Pell solution generates infinitely many more
items.strategy: Fix one nonzero solution and multiply it by $\varepsilon_D^k$ for all integers $k$. The norm stays fixed by multiplicativity, and the positive real embedding changes strictly with $k$, so the resulting solutions are distinct.

title: Pell Equations and Generalized Pell Orbits — Examples

items.title: The Pell and negative Pell equations for $D=2$
items.strategy: Compute the period $[1;\overline{2}]$, extract the norm $-1$ solution $1 + \sqrt{2}$, square it to obtain the fundamental norm-one solution $3 + 2\sqrt{2}$, and list the first several powers.

items.title: The Pell equation for $D=3$
items.strategy: Compute the even period of $\sqrt{3}$, identify the least norm-one convergent, and use the parity criterion to show that $x^2 - 3y^2 = -1$ has no integral solution.

items.title: The negative Pell equation for $D=5$
items.strategy: Use the odd period of $\sqrt{5}$ to locate the least solution of $x^2 - 5y^2 = -1$, then square it to obtain the least positive solution of $x^2 - 5y^2 = 1$.

items.title: The Pell equation for $D=14$
items.strategy: Reuse the NT-7 complete-quotient states for $\sqrt{14}$, locate the first returned state, and apply the norm identity to identify the first convergent with norm $1$.

items.title: The large fundamental solution for $D=61$
items.strategy: Compute the period data for $\sqrt{61}$, identify the convergent prescribed by the parity criterion, and use it to illustrate that the least solution can be enormous even though the continued-fraction algorithm is finite.

items.title: Generalized Pell orbits for $x^2 - 6y^2 = 3$
items.strategy: Start from the representative $3 + \sqrt{6}$ and the Pell generator $5 + 2\sqrt{6}$, then verify that every solution lies in one of the resulting orbits under multiplication by powers of $5 + 2\sqrt{6}$.

items.title: Bounded representatives for $x^2 - 7y^2 = 57$
items.strategy: Apply the explicit orbit bounds to $x^2 - 7y^2 = 57$, enumerate the finitely many representatives in that box, and regenerate the full solution set from those representatives by powers of the fundamental Pell unit.

items.title: A generalized Pell solution need not be a convergent
items.strategy: Use a sourced solution such as $3 + \sqrt{6}$ or $8 + \sqrt{7}$, check that its rational quotient is not among the convergents of the relevant square root, and explain that the missing hypothesis is the small-norm bound behind the convergent criterion.

items.title: The elementary Pell order can miss units from the larger quadratic order
items.strategy: Use $D = 5$ and compare $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{5}]$ with the larger explicit order $\mathbb{Z}[(1 + \sqrt{5})/2]$. The unit $(1 + \sqrt{5})/2$ has norm $-1$ and lies outside $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{5}]$, which keeps the NT-8 seam visible without using any theorem about maximal orders.
